notes.title: New Kaiserpunk Playtest is around the corner
notes.content:
[h2]Hello,[/h2]

This week, from [b]Friday Nov 29th until Dec 3rd[/b], a public Playtest, second one, will be held for Kaiserpunk. This game features a full production chain city builder mechanics combined with many grand strategy elements, all set in an alternative history of the first half of the 20th century.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/4a0d1b4a42c694dd85efbc99a73037f15bbb2c0c.jpg[/img]

Rebuild your own city and territory, set up production and logistics, then take your success to the global stage and spread order to over 100 world regions. Tools of getting there can be pure military conquest, diplomacy or economic domination, whichever suits you best.

This is the second Playtest for Kaiserpunk and playable version will be [b]much more completed than the demo several months back[/b]. There is still much work to be done but this version should clearly showcase what the game is all about.

You can apply for the Playtest through simple [i]Request Access[/i] button [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2012190/KAISERPUNK/]on the Kaiserpunk store page[/url] and access will be granted when Playtest officially starts on [b]November 29th[/b].

Take a look, give it a spin and give us any feedback you'd like to share with devs. You can do so on Steam, Discord ( https://discord.gg/6FfVfPfDNz ) or email kaiserpunk_support@overseer-publishing.com .

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/eafff751bbae5a1085cab07f7378352179bd397d.jpg[/img]

Any and all constructive feedback to help complete this complex game is truly appreciated. Besides adding a lot of recently completed features, feedback from first Playtest also impacted many changes and improvements to previous features. Feedback from this Playtest will help improve the game further.

Just a few significant additions you can expect in this round of Playtest:
[list]
[*][b]Flag design[/b] – You're leading a new nation, you should have a flag…your own designed flag
[*][b]Selection of heritages[/b] – German, Western allies, Russian… choose your starting heritage
[*][b]Social pillars[/b] – set your political alignment
[*][b]Tutorial 2.0[/b] - sections completely reworked based on player input from earlier Playtest
[*][b]Maps[/b] – over 20 maps available through 4 different geographical biomes
[*][b]More stories[/b] – multiple new stories with players choices and mutual causality
[*][b]Diplomacy system[/b] – If that's your strong side, war isn't the only option anymore
[*][b]Basic trade system[/b] – can't find and produce all the riches on your own? Trade for them!
[*][b]Tier 3 production chains and buildings[/b] – build more, build bigger
[*][b]Reworked world map HUD[/b] – previous feedback from players gave us many ideas for improvements, so voila
[*][b]UI/UX 2.0[/b] – what can we say? It's much better
[*][b]Army specializations[/b]
[*][b]Army units and buildings up to Tier 3[/b] (out of 4 in total)
[*][b]Decorations system[/b] (2 out of 3 tiers finished) – much bigger city you can now build needs to be shown off, right?

notes.title: Revealing Update v.1.500.0 – community requested QoL box of goodies
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello to all of you, Sea Mayors! [/b][/i]

As promised a little while ago, today we’re releasing a [b]second part of community frequently requested improvements[/b] for Aquatico. Some of these things have been mentioned soon after the game released, so we apologize for the delay. Combining all updates that came after release, there were a [b]LOT[/b] of changes so we had to make priorities for each individual update. Hope everyone seeking the specific elements found in this update won’t hold it against us for having to wait a little bit. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/666f0b0fccf5e1ead2c4f9b75a923cee11cf4733.jpg[/img]

The center point of the upgrade to [b]v.1500.0[/b] are [b]numerous QoL game elements[/b]. They range from introducing new gameplay features to further pinpointing next optimization avenues. Before listing the specific technical changelog, a few words on what changes include:

[i][u][b]Research stacking[/b][/u][/i] – this was asked by a huge number of players, and these requests were completely legit. Given the sheer number of researches available, and their importance in timely development of your colony, you were right to ask for an easier and quicker way to organize your steps. From now, when you decide which research to start next, you can click a few of them in advance. If you select more then one research, each one will get a numerical designation (what is first to be researched, then second and so on…). These researches will then be executed in a designated sequence. Should you wish to cancel the selected sequence, simply click on second research in line to cancel it, then you can reselect the new sequence. If some research is yet unavailable, you’ll be prompted it cannot go to currently selected sequence.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/6a43670b6f62946d14db86fd5499d8829215ea97.jpg[/img]

[i][u][b]Further optimizations[/b][/u][/i] – after several rounds of global optimization runs (on background gameplay calculations and some graphics corrections), we’re now taking it deeper to objects, models and textures. Main aim is to further slash the memory requirements and to improve performance in later game stages.

[i][u][b]Additional Steam achievements[/b][/u][/i] – ever since we’ve added bigger chunks of additional gameplay layers (expeditions, Atlantis project missions, derelicts…), many of you asked for an additional Steam achievements that would validate the completion of these additional tasks. So, in this update, we’re including 7 new Steam achievements – Atlantis Project, The final chapter, Lord of the sea, The scavenger, The scavengers King, The protector, Master of disaster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/22dc2d136cdf9eb46aeac7aa7d9480e9a9b84a81.jpg[/img]

[i][u][b]QoL suggested improvements[/b][/u][/i] – this time we’re including tweaks to severity of people leaving colony due to lack of food tiers and variety. Also, deselection mouse option is now present to avoid accidental mis-clicks with wrong option activated, then addition of framerate limiter to options, improvements to photo mode and camera interactions, overlapping of map opening with notification icons, and many more details you’ll notice during your play-sessions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/150f302dc6740b40334afa17e7e2df1a9d4499fc.jpg[/img]

It is our sincere hope that this update will make your playtime more cozy and your colony planning more straightforward. We wish to demonstrate that [b]Aquatico is being refined every day and will continue to be refined[/b], and more importantly, that we’re present on every community channel we have and [b]will continue listening to what you have to say[/b]. [u][b]Thank you[/b][/u] for huge amount of ideas and suggestions we received in past few months. Many of them found their way into post-release updates already, and many more are yet to be discussed, designed and introduced in future updates!

[b]CHANGELOG[/b]
[list]
[*] ADDED: Research stacking – select several researches in advance to initiate an entire automatic research sequence
[*] ADDED: New Steam achievements linked to post-release added gameplay content
[*] ADDED: Framerate limiter slider in the options menu
[*] OPTIMIZATION: A number of additional 3D models
[*] OPTIMIZATION: Improvements to performance in later stages of the game when colony is bigger 
[*] IMPROVED: Pace of colonists leaving colony due to food related issues is now decreased
[*] FIXED: Dome upper hull doesn’t disappear with camera zooming in photo mode
[*] FIXED: Overlapping of map and notification icons when accessing expeditions is corrected
[*] TWEAKED: Right mouse click deselection of previously activated option
 [/list]

notes.title: Getting started video for new players + status report on next update
notes.content:
[i][b]Hi good people of the undersea![/b][/i]

Few weeks ago we've made and released a video called „Tips & Tricks“ with some suggestions and best practices to tackle mid to later game challenges in Aquatico. Since there are  a number of fresh players coming into game, we've decided to make [b]another video more focused on first couple of ingame years[/b].

In this video we're covering the [b]initial tasks you should be mindful[/b] in the early game. There are only a few possible „hardships“ that can hamper your advance in first couple of years, and in this video you can see several ways to help yourself get a good headstart. It's always tricky in early game because you tackle lack of resources and lack of manpower at the same time. However, start of the game also offers some opportunities that aren't present later, so the better you use these early opportunities, the easier it will be going forward.

You'll see all the details in the video itself, but some [b]highlights[/b] for early game would be the following:

-	[b]Try planning ahead[/b]. When underwater colony is still small, you have a chance to set the stage for all subsequent development. Observe the grid view and determine where your future locations for extracting certain resources will be. Plan the pipeline system and be mindful that this system will eventually be very extensive. Note that certain buildings have bonuses when contructed near some other building

-	If you're low on resources, and you can't yet produce everything you need, remember there are number of essential [b]resources that can be scooped from the environment[/b] in early game – plastics, iron, stone, various advanced resources from dismantling derelicts on the seabed. If you decide to pick up a lot of these resources, make sure you have additional depots to store them

-	To avoid severe worker/drone shortages in early stages of the game, [b]try conducting as many upgrades[/b] to production buildings as you possibly can. These will significantly increase efficiency without the need to dramatically increase worker numbers

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sFiI0Fh2JqQ

Aquatico is a game where dozens of elements are interlinked, and you'd be surprised how big of a difference [b]good foundations[/b] can have on longer playsessions. If you set up everything smoothly and efficiently, you'll always have enough time and resources to tackle advanced challenges that come later. And viceversa – unefficiently created basic layout can cause chained hickups later, and it is always harder to reorganize already existing colony then to try making it work from earliest stages.

When it comes to other things we've been working on – in about a week we'll be releasing [b]second part of „community suggested“ improvements[/b]. In next update that will include the [b]upgrade to research system[/b] that will allow for stacking of multiple researches in advace, [b]additional Steam achievements[/b] linked to new content introduced after release, [b]another batch of memory and graphics optimizations[/b] and more…

[i][b]That's it from us on this fine Thursday. Have fun and see you next week with next update![/b][/i]

notes.title: Update 1.200.1 – Batch of frequently requested improvements
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello Sea Mayors,[/b][/i]

As many of you already came to expect, another weekend is approaching, and we have [b]yet another update[/b] ready for you.

For this occasion we’ve dived into list of improvements and suggestions that originated from our discussions with players. [b]Next two updates will mostly contain your own suggestions[/b], but few things are  little bit more work so they will wait another week or so. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/cf6e4da8cba3b0d706ecf932e69c51c038adff3b.jpg[/img]

Anyways, back to today’s content – one of the biggest changes is [b]relocating of your citizens[/b]. As your underwater colony expands and you create new workplaces, there is a need for people to change places of residence and have them live closer to their jobs. System that controlled this already existed, but based on you feedback it was insufficient. For that reason, relocation system has been reworked and this process will now be faster and more precise. It will allow your production chains to work more efficiently and adapt to any change better.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/807f73a1b6c9b803855134049198974f6bf29c4c.jpg[/img]

Another frequently asked change was the [b]display of main resources[/b] on the main game screen. With changes made today, [b]resources displayed on main HUD are grouped into categories,[/b] similar to how various “tools” items are shown under tools section. If you hover your mouse over each resource, you’ll see not only that specific resource, but several other that are similar or belong to the same frequently used category. Basically, every resource that you’ll need often (whether they are some resources needed for construction of building upgrades), will now be displayed on the main screen and there is no need to constantly open depot manifests to look for the current status of each individual resource.

From other update elements, few bugs with expedition system have been resolved and we’ve continued the [b]optimization[/b] work on numerous building models.
 
[b]CHANGELOG[/b]

[list]
[*] REVAMPED: Relocation of citizens – your people will now move between houses and places of residence in dependence of where they work, cutting travel time and making worker efficiency better  
[*] TWEAKED: Tidal turbines will now accurately display movement in accordance to tide movements
[*] IMPROVED: Frequently used resources are now displayed in groups on the main HUD making it easier to find and track them constantly
[*] FIXED: Expedition world map and local colony view are now properly separated avoiding errors in selections and navigation
[*] FIXED: Error where expedition mission objective wanted to remove too many batteries from stock is now corrected
[*] FIXED: A number of text errors corrected
[*] OPTIMIZED: Several additional object models optimized for better performance
[/list]

Hope you’ll like the changes, and we’re off to second part of community suggested tweaks. That update you can expect in just over a week time!

[i][b]Have a nice weekend! [/b][/i]

notes.title: Assistance for later game content - some tips & tricks
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings Sea Mayors![/h1]

Today we don't have an update, but while next batch of improvements is being worked at, there is something we wanted to cover a little bit.

From a large amount of data we received by players in recent months, we realized our players out there are employing s lot of very different tactics to complete goals in Aquatico. That is perfectly ok, we left the game open intentionally so players can use all sorts of tactics to advance through the game. 

Looking at your playthroughs we also learned a lot about various possibilities, about what you prefer, like or dislike. And we also learned about several mechanics that some of you find more difficult then others

To address these difficulties, we tried to cover several [b]tips & tricks[/b] in following video. They are related to mid and later game content, and to cover early game difficulties we'll be preparing another video concentrated at first couple of ingame years alone.

A few highlights among advices for later game content would revolve around a [b]single point – plan ahead[/b]. Once your underwater city becomes extensive, number of challenges will increase, but if everything is properly set, you shouldn't be in too much trouble:

-	While you'll probably have sufficient space to physically expnd your city on most maps, beware of how you expand. Some buildings have bonuses related to other buildings, resources are dependent on depot and warehouses locations… As your city grows, distances can become more troublesome and workers and drones spend more and more time going between larger distances. Place your depots strategically, relative to sources of produced gooda and places of consumption

-	By later game, you'll be fully aware of your consumption, but when you expand production further, don't overdo it. Sometimes attempts to secure a very comfortable excess of some resource can lead to shortage of something else, or to a shortage of drones producing them

-	When you build in upper domes section, be mindful that at one point you'll likely have a lot of independent domes. People will need to travel between them to use various amenities. It's unlikely you'll have everything in a single dome, so plan to buil a connections via cable car between domes

-	Multiple underwater farms will likely be a necessity, and if that is the case, it is wise to randomize what farms are producing. More various food resources can open a path to more complex products, and amend the emerging needs for advanced food diversity later on

-	As your city becomes bigger, your pipeline system will expand too. Creating an automated repair building for pipelines is highly recommended

-	There are also some options that you might not want to explore too early. For example, when you build an expedition house, expedition submarines become available. Each expedition you send will be a drain to your resources until they complete their task. Remember that before you commit to explore beyond your colony

-	If you end up in trouble regarding any of your resources or production chains, don't forget you can always adjust your input/output by temporarily shutting down any building or reallocating production elsewhere

-	When colony is large and contains dozens of buildings, remember you can paint each one individually, or paint all buildings of the same type in a certain manner. It helps finding your way around

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bveatbOBZSY

Hopefully, some of you will find this useful. We're looking forward to your continuous feedback!

[i][b]Maintain your oxygen level and until next time![/b][/i]

notes.title: Introducing multiple game modes + Atlantis storyline
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings Sea Mayors![/h1]

Today is a great day to finally release a [b]second part of our major update[/b] for Aquatico. We’ve already announced s few major elements of this expansion, but complete package is now here!

Since we’re mostly talking about pure additional [b]game content[/b] here, it took us a little bit longer to prepare and test everything, but we are excited to finally share everything we did in recent weeks and months. Crucial goal with today’s update was to [b]expand the gameplay[/b], add more value and replayability to your experience and also allow broader insight into overall backstory and goals you’re attempting to achieve in your underwater adventure. 

Let us walk you through some of the highlights from today’s menu:

[b]GAME MODES[/b]
[u]When starting a new game[/u], you’ll now have a selection of [b]three different game modes[/b]. Each is different in terms of what is available and expected during gameplay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/43814ecfb01512f33e92da23a6fad7966eccd87f.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Sandbox mode[/b][/u] is pretty much the “regular” game mode familiar from previous game version (all game rules apply, resources have to be secured and managed for the success of your own colony, and all challenges are present).

[b][u]Storyline mode[/u][/b] is basically sandbox mode + Atlantis Project campaign (all game rules apply, resources have to be secured and managed for the success or your own colony, as well as for participation in construction of Atlantis Project, all challenges are present).

[b][u]Creative mode[/u][/b] is something completely different. It’s a mode that allows players to fully explore the lengths of their imagination by simply having an option to build the underwater vision unhampered by anything (game rules are modified, resources are infinite, people/drones replenished as needed, all researches and buildings are open, challenges and disasters are disabled).

[b]ATLANTIS PROJECT CAMPAIGN[/b]
This is essentially a [b]long quest chain[/b] that spans through the entire game. It is available [u]only when starting a new game and selecting Storyline mode[/u]. Atlantis Project questline will become available the moment you [u]research and build your Expedition house[/u] and get an option to explore global underwater map. On that map you’ll have access to start the Atlantis campaign with all of the missions it includes. Missions are [u]manually accepted[/u] so you can execute them whenever you feel you’re ready. Before you accept these missions, make sure your logistics can support it without causing too much problems for your own colony.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/3de9c50ed2d6615a427b36305fe18cc14e65ab53.png[/img]

Without spoiling too much, suffice to say that Atlantis Project is an incredible endeavor led jointly by all scattered underwater colonies. There are many such colonies created after chaos engulfed Earth surface, and underwater city player is building is only one such colony. Even your colony wasn’t the first attempt at this on your specific location (there are previous failed attempts that you can see from derelicts across the sea floor). Atlantis missions include separated [b]objectives[/b], introduce players to some specific [b]new characters[/b], add several [b]unique researches[/b] and ultimately, if fully completed, brings the satisfaction of creating something capable of ensuring a lasting future of humanity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/f9b8168820fe1702559f270b2076089c7bf79e5e.jpg[/img]

To better explain what Atlantis is all about, we've made a short video with some additional details:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evLvYBLCOgE 

In purely technical terms, today’s update also introduces new voiceovers, some new cutscenes, new sub-selections in buildings menu, refinement to recently added new biome maps and a new map, additional balancing tweaks and ofcourse a bunch of improvements to existing features as well as bugfixes…

[b]CHANGELOG[/b]
[list]
[*] ADDED: 3 different game modes for new game: Sandbox, Storyline, Creative 
[*] ADDED: Atlantis Project campaign system
[*] ADDED: New character portraits related to Atlantis missions
[*] ADDED: New voiceovers related to Atlantis missions
[*] ADDED: New global map location related to management of Atlantis Project objectives
[*] ADDED: New researches linked to progression and unlocking of Atlantis missions
[*] ADDED: Several new cutscenes
[*] ADDED: Additional new map in recently added Polar biome
[*] ADDED: Colony advisor character to assist in certain stages of the game
[*] ADDED: New separate tab for Energy production buildings only
[*] IMPROVED: Upgrade bonuses display info now has correct calculation and gives more precise information to player
[*] IMPROVED: Rebalancing of environment points requirements by individual citizens
[*] IMPROVED: Hotel building stats and useability tweaked
[*] IMPROVED: Intro cutscene on Polar biome map 
[*] FIXED: Numerous text and language errors, as well as several reported visual glitches
[/list]
 
We’d also like to mention that almost entire content for this update was crafted [b]based on suggestions and feedback[/b] we received from players. [u][b]Thank you[/b][/u] for your continuous input, it really has been invaluable! 

And naturally, all of the improvements released today aren’t the end. There are more things in the pipeline and updates will continue into the coming weeks and months!

[i][b]Enjoy the update and until next time,
Stay well and keep monitoring your oxygen levels!
Digital Reef Games team[/b][/i]

notes.title: Sneak peek into next major update
notes.content:
[i][b]Greetings again, Sea Mayors![/b][/i]

This week we don't have an actual update, mainly because a very large update is in preparation, so we don't want to interrupt our work on that beauty before everything is ready.

But we did want to share some details on the first important part of that update - so called [u][b]"Creative" mode[/b][/u].
Many of you will recognize this from dozens of your suggestions we received in weeks following the game's release. So, since you wanted it so much, we've decided it really can be a very good addition to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/e3db874f0a4e8833cde304a0f7a2bc42d6b0beba.jpg[/img]

[b][u][i]What exactly is the creative mode?[/i][/u][/b] 
Well, the creative mode is one of [u][b]three main game modes[/b][/u] that will be unlocked with the next major update. All of these modes will be selectable when you start a new game. And creative mode sets a specific game conditions and rules. Basically, when playing in creative mode, [b]challenges are turned off[/b] (shark attacks, pirate attacks, megalodons), your [b]resources are infinite[/b], and your [b]citizens/drones will always be replenished[/b] to any needed number. In addition, [b]the research tree will be fully completed[/b] and therefore, all [b]buildings and options will be available from the first minute[/b] of your play-session,

Your only task will be to [b]unleash your imagination[/b] to the full extent and build your own paradise beneath the waves. You'll have [u][b]no limits[/b][/u], you can build anything anywhere and your only concern will be to make the wildest possible vision of your underwater city, unrestricted by any game rules, resource shortages or citizen happiness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/6e8f7d85bcdd8cf93b727154b5297b3186f8bc57.jpg[/img]

We're confident you'll have plenty of ideas what to create in this mode, and [b]hopefully you'll share your creations[/b] with the other players too!

In other news - the second part of the incoming major update, [b]Atlantis Project[/b] is entering final testing soon. Its introduction requires some changes to balancing variables, and since many players have wildly different ways to play Aquatico, it is necessary to find a fine balance for everyone.

We are hugely excited to bring you all these additions, and we're positive they will enhance your game experience significantly, both when using "serious" game mode with all the rules in place, and when using creative mode to construct your insane visions.

[i][b]Until next time!
Keep an eye on your oxygen levels![/b][/i]

notes.title: First of two major content expansions arrived! - version 1.010.1
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello Sea Mayors, some great news today! [/b][/i]

Today we're starting to roll out the first of the bigger [b]content updates[/b] for Aquatico. Elements of this update will start [b]expanding the gameplay[/b] itself, and most building blocks grew from thousands of your forum messages, emails and Discord suggestions. The main goal is to enhance the overall play experience, establish closer links to the backstory and the apocalyptic setting, and to set the stage for future in-game objectives.

Since we can't immediately change or add everything, we've decided to first improve and expand areas of the game that you had the most suggestions about. And in these two updates the content will revolve around immersion, links to general setting and objectives, both short term and global game objective.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/6c7977083ca50b55b3bc0603249d8ff1d39d53a8.jpg[/img]

[b][u]Some of these changes will be visible only if you start a fresh game[/u][/b]. For example, when starting a new game, you'll now see more a direct connection to the background story, how and why you ended up on the ocean floor. Additionally, map scenery has been upgraded with submerged buildings and objects describing the new reality and the elevated water levels.

Also, since [b]your underwater colony is not the first one[/b], you will encounter the [b]remains of previous failed settlement attempts[/b], like abandoned and ruined parts of underwater constructions. There is a new game mechanics allowing for the deconstruction and reuse of valuable resources from them. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/d8019f76406c0fbb1253c051e6548fb48e7bc23b.jpg[/img]

Throughout the game, you'll now have references to events happening in the world globally, the progress of other underwater colonies, and how far you are from achieving main goal – the completion of [b]Atlantis Project[/b]. Basically, Atlantis project is a mega construction project aimed at creating a huge underwater megalopolis, the center for all dispersed underwater colonies in this new post apocalyptic world.

Each underwater colony, like the one you're leading yourself in Aquatico, is tasked with gathering survivors, creating a self-sustainable habitat and ensuring the production of resources. In time, each colony will be contributing these resources (both material resources and human resources) to the construction of Atlantis in its full glory. Main goal of the game will be to finish the Atlantis Project and spark the complete revitalization of human civilization, but more on that in the next major content update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/96209a29647587ac282e1ba82dc57d25dd08cc86.jpg[/img]

Chunks of all this is part of today's update, while the second part will come in second content update in about a month.

Besides these elements, this update also contains a couple of additional game maps, new or updated panels, the next rebalance package, modifications of resource tiers, addition of citizen discussions and opinions (visible in small text bubbles) and many other background details.

notes.title: Dev Diary: Expeditions and exploration
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello Sea people![/b][/i]

The fifth developer video is here, and we're talking about [i][b][u]Expeditions[/u][/b][/i] this time. Now, bear in mind that Expeditions are one of the non essential features in Aquatico, meaning you don't have to build or use them at all throughout the game, but at some point they can be a very useful tool to expand quicker.

[i][u][b]How do you access them?[/b][/u][/i]
Expeditions become available when you build an [b]Expedition house[/b]. That building has a dock for your Expedition submarine, and once created, you can access the Expedition panel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/41718348c6c21f290e33808588f200dc8defa13a.jpg[/img]

[i][u][b]How do you use them?[/b][/u][/i]
Once available, you can enter the Expedition panel, and start equipping your submarine with essentials for an expedition. Each submarine will need some people for the [b]crew[/b], some [b]batteries[/b] for submarine power and some [b]food[/b] to sustain them while travelling. The amount that you need of these resources depends on how far you'll be sending your Expedition. When the submarine is well supplied, you can choose any destination on the global expedition map and send your submarine. Once it reaches the destination, you can explore and see what they find, and that can be any number of things: additional survivors, some basic or advanced resources etc...

While an expedition is underway, you'll see an icon on the main game screen showing the quick stats of your Expedition - how far they are from the destination, if something happened during their trip, the status of the remaining resources onboard and so on. If you run out of supplies (and the game will project the required amount of supplies based on the destination set), be careful to [b]send a resupply[/b] craft before your submarine crew perishes.

You can also divert your submarine to a different destination, or choose to head to a next point of interest after the first destination is explored, without returning to base. But if you choose to keep your submarine out there exploring one destination after another, make sure they are always resupplied.

Also note that your submarine can sometimes be intercepted during an Expedition, or some event can trigger during one, so there is always a chance for unexpected thing to happen. 

[i][u][b]Something to pay attention to...[/b][/u][/i]
Expeditions can yield very nice and useful rewards, but beware that [b]Expeditions are costly[/b], especially if you're sending them far away or to multiple destinations. It is wise to send out Expeditions only once you're certain you have enough spare resources to equip and resupply your submarine, otherwise you risk losing both the resources and the crew.

And once you take your submarine for a spin, if you get to a tight spot regarding resources in your colony, you can always recall your Expedition back to home base and let it wait there until the next opportunity.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t8jTbb4OdNs

[i][u][b]Some other news regarding Aquatico development in the past week[/b][/u][/i]
It's been a very dynamic week. We're still on track for Jan 12th release date, we're all very excited and hyped, but we also have a lot of work left to do. We've been improving guard tower weapons, testing shark attacks, making a lot of balancing tweaks, hunting bugs in various places... a very interesting week all things considered.

In any case, that's the update for this week, we're off to the "frontlines" once again, and see you on the big day next week!

notes.title: Dev Diary: Environment and beautification system
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello Sea people![/b][/i]

Next in our Dev Diary series is here, and this time it's about [b]Environment system[/b], beautifications and how to make the best out of it, with least resources.

First of all - [i][b]what is the Environment system?[/b][/i] Well, [b]Environment[/b] is one of the categories that makes the broader [b]Happiness score[/b] of your citizens. In the early game, your entire population will be happy with only the bare necessities - food, fuel and a place to live in the pressurized domes. As your colony grows and expands, people will start demanding more from life. And that's where the Happiness categories come in. There are numerous categories here: [b]safety, religion, education, environment[/b]... Each category has its own points and different mechanics of how to increase these points.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/3c2d6bb5424bffdb355f29a7c62473dfee95666a.jpg[/img]

In today's Dev Diary we're talking specifically about [b]Environment points[/b], since it has arguably the most complex calculation. But it's really pretty simple once you get the general idea.

Environment includes everything that impacts your dome lifestyle: what amenities it offers, how appealing it is to spend time in. Remember that people didn't just choose to go live underwater, they were forced to. And now, they will expect you to offer them a lifestyle as similar to their previous life on the Earth's surface as possible.

[i][b]How do you do that?[/b][/i] Through the beautification building panel. The availability of various beautifications will increase as you unlock them through the [b]research tree[/b]. And each beautification object (fountains, trees, plants, monuments, benches, street lamps, parks etc...) awards a certain number of environment points. Not all beautifications award the same number of points, and even the same [b]beautification object can yield different amount of points [/b]depending on where and how it is placed. 

This means that you can't just unlock the simplest beautification object and stamp dozens of them in one place to gather a bunch of needed points. You need to combine them, plan how to use them and where exactly to place them. In essence, you need to have an idea of how you want your domes organized, not just randomly placing beautifications around. Each object grants some points, but the exact amount depends on proximity of some other beautification object. When placing them, a [b]highlighted number[/b] will be shown of how many points that object will give at a specific location. So, feel free to play around with it a bit before deciding. 

Note that, in some cases, if placed in a completely meaningless way, beautifications can even yield [b]negative points[/b] and decrease the overall Environment standing. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=twyaqDdUjbg

In our Diary video, you'll see how this calculation works and how you can maximize the Environment score in any given situation.

Well, that's it for today, hope this is helpful!
Until next one!

notes.title: Dev Diary: Pressurized Domes and some tricks for managing them
notes.content:
[i][b]Greetings,[/b][/i]

It's time for another quick video Dev diary from us. Today we'll explain a little bit more about the second building layer in Aquatico - the [u][b]Dome section[/b][/u].

In general, your underwater city will consist of two separate and different layers: the sea floor level for mostly industrial production and pipeline infrastructure layout, and the upper Domes level on top of the first one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/9691cdcb3372088e751937c0d3cad6e5f2022171.jpg[/img]

The main difference between them is that "ground" level is exposed to the environment directly, meaning all the work done here must be performed by either mechanical drones, or by people wearing underwater "walker" suits. [b]Domes[/b], on the other side, are [b]fully pressurized[/b] with their own [b]micro environment[/b], meaning inside them your people can live unhindered, with no life support suits. Basically, in Dome section citizens can live very similar to the way they used to live in any surface city before the catastrophe that drove them into the oceans.

In Domes, you also [b]don't need to set up any pipelines[/b] (base pillar of each dome is already connected to the pipeline on the ground level), and here you'll do most of the work to make a good and cozy life for your people - build houses, trade companies, cinemas, restaurants, bars, schools, make parks, plant trees etc...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/6091e191e18753bc848a1922c8c731b7fcf5ed80.jpg[/img]

Note that in the early stages of the game, your Domes will be used mainly for simple housing, all other features of Domes will come in play more and more as you progress. When the population reaches higher numbers and your city becomes more advanced, people will require better living conditions and more amenities. They will also desire a better looking environment to live in, so you'll have plenty of tasks to perform in Domes.

Through research and development, you'll eventually get access to [b]three different sizes of Domes[/b], and at one point you'll essentially have an entire city on top of a city.

Of course, once you expand both layers of your colony, you'll also have an option to build and [b]connect cable cars between Domes[/b]. This transport system allows your people to cross between Domes without the need to descend to the sea floor level, equip underwater suits and head to another dome. There is literally no chance you can build everything necessary in a single dome, so this feature greatly simplifies everything.

Some more details on all of this you can check in our dev video!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wnw4Gp5-o1c&t=23s

Until next time, happy holidays and all the best!

notes.title: Dev Diary: Food system + what we did this week
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello everybody,[/b][/i]

As we did last week, today we'll post another short dev video explaining, this time, some details on [b]food requirements[/b], potential challenges and best ways of handling it. Quick update on the general development progress (I know many of you are curious) will be below.

Food production in Aquatico is among the few things that are [b]existentially important[/b] for your colony and your citizens. Being underwater, they will initially rely on specific nutritional resources found on the sea floor, but as time goes on you will secure ways to produce more and more different types of food, including some typical for conditions on the surface of the planet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/4946be5a8605b31b788e402680fcc7ea0472bcb0.jpg[/img]

In general, there are three things you'll have to manage regarding food, and that goes for the entire game:
[olist]
[*][b]Food quantity[/b]
[*][b]Food variety[/b]
[*][b]Securing all food tiers[/b]
[/olist]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9AI3BBeC01M

In early game, [b]sheer quantity[/b] will be sufficient. Your people aren't demanding too much, so simple gathering buildings should do the trick and get them whatever is necessary for surviving.

In mid game, your people will start seeking more different types of food resources, but still from the same food tier (call it food complexity or "fanciness"). That is indicated by [b]"food variety"[/b] info at the end of each food tier datasheet. In this stage you'll have to start producing different types of food resources yourself. Open access to more advanced food productions and buildings by researching various tech related to farms and mariculture.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/af58f003d834cbddcfe512698056d363efcc6f7f.jpg[/img]

In late game, your people will, for happiness and health reasons, require multiple different food types from all food tiers, so expect to already have tuna cages, greenhouses and buildings for manufacturing specific highly advanced food types (lobsters, sushi etc...)

Demands from people will increase [b]gradually[/b], as you advance through the tech tree and as your population grows. Basic food amount must be met in order to sustain your colony. Later, once you start getting notifications for the lack of food diversity, happiness will start to decrease, but you'll have plenty of time to set up the needed production, or simply buy the missing resources via trade.

[u][b]Development update:[/b][/u]
Yes, we're still on track for the stated release date. This week we've been working mostly on implementing all remaining social points mechanisms (religion, safety etc...), and giving them early balancing. 
We've also been adding "smart tips", a helper tips for players throughout the game that open as you reach certain stages of development.
Next round of optimizations is also underway with optimizing more buildings, pathfinding, level of details and tweaks to processes that present the greatest loads to hardware elements.

Last part of this week's effort was most fun - shooting at sharks and other stuff. It's not perfect yet, but made us a little bit happier already.

[i][b]That's all for today, stay dry and see you next week![/b][/i]

Our first Playtest weekend has passed, and we're still gathering impressions here. In short –[b] it was awesome![/b] Several thousand players got access and tried Aquatico for the first time, and we couldn't be happier with response.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/f71c9bbed1ddcb23dc9398dbbd77d755fa1183e2.jpg[/img]

The very idea of an underwater city building experience seems to resonate strongly with a lot of players out there who were really enjoying the early shown atmospherics and general mood of the game. Since this was only the alpha game version, there were bugs and issues and we're taking into account everything reported back to us. Improvements are already underway, based on feedback and data files you've sent us.

At this moment, our entire team wishes to thank all of you who participated in the Playtest. You gave us a very good idea of what things you enjoy the most, what needs improving, and where the current issues are. Thank you for this invaluable feedback, thank you for all the suggestions and thank you for your time to provide us with the data files.

[u][i][b]What's next?[/b][/i][/u]

For all players who didn't get the chance to try the Playtest version, we are preparing a [u][b]first demo version[/b][/u] of Aquatico! This will already be an improved version of the Playtest build, and that version will continue to be updated as development goes ahead. Expect this demo to be available in time for the Steam Next fest. Note that this demo version will also be an incomplete game, but already one step closer to it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/d636179885c948738f2c4d686a41c58b1ce5a058.png[/img]

And while on the subject of Steam Next Fest – yes, Aquatico will participate in this event, you'll have a chance to view livestreams of the game, grab the demo and give it a spin, and of course – throw additional feedback at us. There is still much more to come and we'll make Aquatico the best experience it can be!

Once again – [b]thank you[/b]!
Digital Reef Games

notes.title: Last day of Playtest in progress
notes.content:
[b]Hi,[/b]

It's been an interesting couple of days, and we've started the final day of our first Aquatico Playtest. SInce a lot of you still register to try out the game, another group of players will be granted access today. Later today, registrations will be closed, and tomorrow Playtest will officially end.

We'd only like to thank again to everyone that participated, and everyone that will still participate today.
Your feedback has been fantastic - you pointed us to good sides of the game, pointed out what needs to improve, and also shared huge amount of suggestions. We'll have an interesting time going through all of the data received, but in the end, this effort will help us make a better experience.

Upgrades to game, based on this feedback have already started to happen, and this will intensify as we make progress to next major milestone - a demo version.

notes.title: Take a deep breath - Aquatico public Playtest started!
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello and Welcome, future Sea people![/b][/i]

You've probably seen our Playtest registration already, so sign up if you haven't already, but today is the day for the real thing!

First playable version of Aquatico is [b]now available[/b] to registered alpha test participants. If you want, there is still time – [b]registrations will be open until first Playtest is concluded[/b] on Sunday, September 18th. But the sooner you enter, the more time you'll have to try out the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/bccd8f3903dfbf97e1afc88da1b76024f2c5824d.jpg[/img]

One added bonus here: we've[b] increased [/b]the one-session time limit [b]from 2 to 3 hours[/b]. After that expires, you can always restart the new game and try something different, as many times as you want.

[b]NOTE[/b] that this is an [b]alpha version[/b], not everything is perfect, and there are some things still missing. Hope it won't ruin your experience too much, we tried to make the initial few hours as complete as possible at this stage, but we also wanted to get you onboard as soon as possible. That gives us more room for improvements and tweaking in the direction that most of you want, and remainder of the development time will serve this cause exactly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/b9092ecdd842a1993e87c88c8d77d29999a2a7b9.jpg[/img]

[i][b][u]YOUR ROLE IN ALL THIS?[/u][/b][/i]
Any of the participants can simply download the alpha version and have some fun with it. But, if you want to add extra value to the full experience offered by Aquatico full game in the future – we ask you to take a more proactive stance and do the following:

[b]1.[/b]	Play carefully and slowly, observe the tutorial hints at the early start so we can decide how much more work these instructions need
[b]2.[/b]	Once you finish your sessions, please retrieve the following files and send them to us at 
        [i][u][b]alphatest@overseer-publishing.com[/b][/u][/i] :
        [b]AquaticoLog.txt[/b] – you can find it in your main game installation directory
        [b]Your save file[/b] – it is .sgs file located in Saves subfolder of your game installation folder
        [b]Dxdiag.txt file[/b] – you can create one by running „dxdiag.exe“ from windows command line

These files will give us ample data to work on upcoming hardware optimizations, difficulty balance, and all other improvements related to game mechanics.

Additionally, you can add a short description of any issues you might experience, any feedback you'd like to share or any suggestion you might have. You can also post the same feedback on Steam forums, or join us at our Discord here: [u][b]https://discord.gg/Sqyms6T2P7[/b][/u]

You can also follow quick news on our Twitter site: [u][b]https://twitter.com/Overseer_Games
[/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/ff970d3a553694f51f25f6a53e1c85b51886b5fe.jpg[/img]

Aquatico is a big project, one we're very excited to work on, and there is still much more work ahead of us. This Playtest will be one of the important pieces of the puzzle we're creating, and your help can be extremely important here.

[b]THANK YOU ALL FOR PARTICIPATING[/b], and we sincerely wish you all have a good time!

[i][b]Don't forget to breathe![/b][/i]
Digital Reef Games & Overseer Games Publishing

notes.title: First public Playtest is right around the corner!
notes.content:
[i][b]Hi everyone![/b][/i]

I know we've been relatively quiet for awhile, but we had good reason to! We've been playing the first Aquatico game version intensely for weeks now, and now that we are happy with the current stage of development, we've decided to include you, the players as well. Your insight and your feedback will be hugely appreciated as we set the next set of goals in this development cycle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/bc2d613604093962ec1045f9081133ae21b58500.jpg[/img]

[b][u]WHAT'S THE DEAL THEN?[/u][/b]
Well, next week, on [b]Friday 16th[/b], we'll open the access to the current version of Aquatico. Access will be opened for the entire weekend ([b]September 16th – September 18th[/b]), and then access will be suspended for now. You're invited to download the build and test the heck out of it. Then spam us with feedback and reactions, we'll take it from there!

[b][u]HOW TO PARTICIPATE?[/u][/b]
We're opening registrations at the time you're reading this announcement. You'll see the register option on the Steam store page, enter the Playtest there, and people registered that way will get access to alpha game version from September 16th until September 18th.

[b][u]WHAT DOES THIS GAME VERSION OFFER?[/u][/b]
Please note that this game version [b]IS NOT[/b] a completed game by any stretch of imagination. Internally, the current development build is more advanced, but in this Playtest version we've opened only the game elements that are sufficiently tested, or game elements that we're most eager to hear your thoughts on.

Entire basic mechanics, resources, production chains, terrain options, multi level construction, pipeline infrastructure, environment scenery, music and sound effects – that's all already in there and you can use it to get the taste of the full experience that is still in the making.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/d09d449678e9515e20def111c89004441dcac07d.jpg[/img]

Some of the things that are still limited: the full stack of maps is not unlocked, the expedition/exploration system is disabled, the event system, higher tier buildings are also locked, more juicy scenery /atmospherics elements, domes (upper construction level) cannot be connected yet via tubes (and an even more advanced transport system within them), more various biomes…

Most importantly – this first game version will be [b]time limited at 2 hours[/b] per play session. You're free to start as many sessions as you'd like, but each will individually be limited to 2 hrs.

As developers, we can tell you that yes, this alpha game version will likely have some bugs and will have some missing elements. If you decide to participate in Playtest, please don’t be annoyed by that, the very purpose of this event is to make sure there are no bugs when release version is reached. There is plenty of finished and enjoyable things already, and your reactions will help us make the entire experience like that – enjoyable.

[b][u]WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THIS PLAYTEST?[/u][/b]
Since we've received a lot of requests by players wanting to check out and test the game, we've decided to use the Steam Playtest feature to do just that, and to do it in a broader and more inclusive way. The game is not yet finished, but it is decently playable and with enough added elements that all your feedback will be very representative and incredible important as strategic guidelines for the remainder of our development time. Plus, after we really enjoyed it - we are especially eager for you to join in and see what we're making here. With your assistance, we can make the game better, a lot better, we're confident of that!

[b][u]WHAT WOULD WE LIKE YOU TO DO AS PLAYTEST PARTICIPANTS?[/u][/b]
The first request we have is easy: opt into the playtest, download the version once it’s available, play it and (hopefully) enjoy it. Feel free to utilize any of the game mechanics as you see fit. Tutorial guidelines will be available, but approach to possible paths is pretty open, and there are multiple ways to organize things in your underwater city. The more you experiment, the better feedback we’ll have. And in turns, that will lead to better game down the road.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/a1f004c2d96b927f305e6650a20aebedc4e37b8b.jpg[/img]

Second thing is – please report your feedback to us, and if you experience any technical difficulties, please report that too. We’ll announce the exact procedure for this next week, but it will be simple and easy.

And lastly – our entire team says a big [b]THANK YOU[/b] in advance, for your participation, for your time invested and for your help in making Aquatico the best it can possibly be!

Welcome!
Digital Reef Games

notes.title: First alpha gameplay trailer
notes.content:
[b][i]Hello to all future Sea people![/i][/b]

Since the initial reveal of Aquatico, we’ve been keeping quiet, but lots of things have been happening on the development front. We saw your reactions to the showcased parts of the game and potential desires for future development elements. And we’re happy to say that many of the things correctly mentioned in Steam and Discord discussions by the emerging community were already in the production pipeline.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/a4e5bf06d3ffeda4dfa766c62d4260a9f383d2b0.jpg[/img]

So the time has come to make another video displaying ongoing progress and reveal a few completely new features in the game - the first alpha gameplay footage!

https://youtu.be/G_-0H6gS1DE

A few of the highlights:

[i][u][b]Vertical layered construction[/b][/u][/i] – your underwater city will have more than one vertical stage for building. The sea-bed level will hold the basic infrastructure, production and industry buildings, while the upper stages enclosed in massive domes will hold housing and other public buildings.

[i][u][b]Underwater infrastructure[/b][/u][/i] – creating a city in an underwater environment comes with its own set of challenges, and to cover these, players will build specific types of infrastructure that supply the needed resources and resolve unique requirements of living in the deep ocean.

[i][u][b]Expedition mechanics[/b][/u][/i] – being previously uninhabited, the ocean floor hides many secrets and the expeditions are there to help you uncover some of them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42281691/1cbf1933c9b2fb2b27f082847266750a3e5f2a8e.jpg[/img]

There are a few more yet unseen game details in the video, but we'll leave it to you if you spot them or not!

This first alpha gameplay video should bring you closer to the very essence of Aquatico, the bedrock fundamentals of how the game will eventually play. A LOT more is coming, and we’ll keep you all updated. The main aim for us here is to achieve both a proper visual display of underwater life, as well as offering a really compelling feeling of how a unique task building an underwater city actually is.

If you're excited as much as we are, [u][b]WISHLIST[/b][/u] and [u][b]FOLLOW[/b][/u] us!

Until next round of news!
